successCriteria.description: src/modules/notification/notification.model.ts defines a Notification entity whose fields are exactly id: string, recipientId: string, type: string, title: string, message: string, relatedEntityType: string | null, relatedEntityId: string | null, status: NotificationStatus, createdAt: Date, readAt: Date | null — with status typed as the shared NotificationStatus enum imported from src/shared/types (not a locally re-declared enum).

The model separates caller-supplied input from generated fields: id, createdAt and readAt are generated by the repository and never caller-supplied; a distinct create/input type carries only the caller-supplied fields (recipientId, type, title, message, relatedEntityType, relatedEntityId, and optionally status).

src/modules/notification/notification.repository.ts defines INotificationRepository with create, findByRecipient, findByEntity, updateStatus and markRead, plus a concrete NotificationRepository implementing it using raw pg parameterized SQL against the shared pool (no Knex/ORM in queries).

Write methods (create, updateStatus, markRead) accept an optional PoolClient as their LAST parameter and fall back to the shared pool when omitted; read methods (findByRecipient, findByEntity) always use the shared pool.

The repository maps snake_case columns (recipient_id, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, created_at, read_at) to the camelCase entity via a private mapRow helper and a *_COLUMNS constant listing the select/returning columns, mirroring the sibling audit/employee/policy/balance repositories.
create persists a row to the notifications table and returns the mapped Notification with a generated id, status defaulting to PENDING when not supplied, createdAt set to now, and readAt null.
markRead sets read_at to now and status to READ for the identified notification; updateStatus persists the supplied NotificationStatus value. Both reject a missing row with a typed not-found error.

constraints: Only src/modules/notification/notification.model.ts and src/modules/notification/notification.repository.ts are in scope for this sub-phase; no service, controller, routes, index.ts, or test files may be created here.
No background fanout or BullMQ; the repository performs only synchronous SQL against the shared pool.
All SQL must be raw pg parameterized queries (no Knex/ORM); no inline SQL outside the repository layer.

The repository must not import a pool, client, or module-level db helper other than the shared pool from src/shared/db; it must not open transactions (no BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK) — transaction orchestration belongs to the service layer via IUnitOfWork.
The module must import NotificationStatus from src/shared/types (re-exported from src/shared/types/index.ts) rather than declaring a new enum.
outOfScope: Unit/integration tests (tests/unit/modules/notification/*.spec.ts) — owned by Phase 6c; this sub-phase must not create test files or gate on test coverage.
Background notification fanout / BullMQ queue processing.
Notification controller, routes, or any HTTP/API surface.

entityInvariants.invariant: status is always one of the shared NotificationStatus values (PENDING | SENT | READ | ARCHIVED); a newly created notification is PENDING unless the caller supplies a status, and readAt is null until the notification is marked read.
id and createdAt are generated by the repository (id via randomUUID, createdAt = now) and are never caller-supplied; readAt is repository-managed and set only by markRead.
relatedEntityType and relatedEntityId are either both present or both null (they identify the same related entity); recipientId references an existing employees.id.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Persists a notification and returns the mapped entity; generates id/createdAt, defaults status to PENDING and readAt to null. Takes an optional PoolClient as the last parameter to join a caller's transaction.
Returns all notifications for a recipient ordered deterministically (e.g. createdAt DESC, id); always uses the shared pool and never accepts a client.
Returns notifications matching a related entity type + id; always uses the shared pool and never accepts a client.
Persists a supplied NotificationStatus for an identified notification; throws a typed not-found error when no row matches; takes an optional PoolClient as the last parameter.
Sets readAt to now and status to READ for an identified notification; throws a typed not-found error when no row matches; takes an optional PoolClient as the last parameter.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Import NotificationStatus from the shared types module (re-exported by src/shared/types/index.ts) rather than declaring a new enum; the values must be exactly PENDING, SENT, READ, ARCHIVED.

Use the shared pg Pool exported from src/shared/db (re-exported by src/shared/db/index.ts) as the default connection; write methods accept an optional PoolClient as the last parameter and fall back to the shared pool.

Match the notifications table contract: snake_case columns id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at; PK id; FK recipient_id -> employees.id; indexes on recipient_id, status, and related_entity_type/related_entity_id.

Reuse RepositoryError and UniqueConstraintError from the employee module's public entry point (src/modules/employee/index.ts) rather than re-declaring them; add only a notification-specific not-found error locally.

Mirror the sibling repository pattern: private mapRow converting snake_case rows to camelCase entities, a *_COLUMNS constant, raw pg parameterized SQL, and the interface + concrete class co-located in the repository file.

integrationPoints.why: The Notification entity's status field is typed with the shared enum; no local enum is declared.
The repository's default connection for all queries; write methods fall back to it when no PoolClient is supplied.
The notification repository reuses the shared error base classes from the employee module's public entry point.
recipientId references employees.id; the FK enforces referential integrity for notification recipients.
